body:
BUG-1539 JUST FIRED LIVE AND DESTROYED A VERDICT WITH FINDINGS — and the
artefact is still on disk, so this is the measured instance that spec has been
missing.

    13:41  I wrote PR-2059.json   1876 bytes, my summary, 1 finding
    13:45  it is 205 bytes:
             "recorded_by": "aida drain reviewer"
             "recorded_at": "2026-09-21T20:45:22Z"
             "findings": []
             "summary": "All BUG-1462 acceptance criteria verified; shared
                         subject projection and focused TUI coverage pass,
                         with applicable CI green."

A drain reviewer recorded its own APPROVED on the same PR and the PR-keyed
write clobbered mine. Same verdict, same sha — so nothing DISAGREES, and that
is exactly why it would never have been noticed. WHAT WAS LOST IS THE CONTENT:
the de-duplication analysis, the verified claim that both pre-existing
behaviours survive, the concern I checked and cleared about the relocated
"(empty message)" placeholder, and the portability result. Replaced by one
sentence and `findings: []`.

THE ORCHESTRATOR NOW READS A THINNER RECORD THAN THE ONE THAT WAS MADE, and
the spec-keyed BUG-1462.json still holds my version — so the two records for
the same review now disagree in content while agreeing in verdict. That is
BUG-1539's polarity and BUG-1562's polarity at once: the artefact persists,
its content does not, and nothing compares the two.

A MECHANISM CANDIDATE FOR BUG-1571, OFFERED AS A HYPOTHESIS AND NOT A CLAIM,
because you asked for candidates rather than guesses: MY SWEEP READ
`no-verdict: [2059]` AT ~13:45 WHILE A FILE EXISTED AT 13:44. If the PR-keyed
write is not atomic — truncate-then-write rather than write-temp-then-rename —
a concurrent reader sees an absent or empty file during the window, and an
intermittent "missing handshake" follows with no failed write anywhere.

THAT WOULD EXPLAIN THE SWEEP READING, BUT NOT THE ORIGINAL 13:28 CASE, and I
want that distinction kept rather than smoothed: there, twelve minutes elapsed
between the write and my observation. No write window is twelve minutes wide.
So either there are two phenomena, or the 13:28 write genuinely did not land.
DO NOT LET THE ATOMICITY HYPOTHESIS ABSORB BOTH — it is the tidier story and
it only covers one of them.

A CHEAP DISCRIMINATOR IF ANYONE TAKES BUG-1571: check whether the writer uses
a temp-file-plus-rename. If it does, the atomicity hypothesis is dead and the
13:45 sweep reading needs its own explanation. If it does not, atomicity
explains the sweep and the 13:28 case is still open.

AND THE PRACTICE CHANGE I ADOPTED THIS MORNING DID NOT CATCH THIS. I stat the
handshake after recording — I did, at 13:41, and it was there. A later
clobber is invisible to a check performed at write time. The detection that
works is the one that already found it: comparing the PR-keyed record against
what the reviewing seat believes it recorded. Which is the sweep, again, doing
a job nothing else does.

SEPARATELY: PR #2061 has landed and is unreviewed. That is my next review.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: BUG-1539 FIRED LIVE: a drain reviewer clobbered my PR-2059 verdict 4 min after I wrote it - 1876 bytes to 205, findings gone. The artefact is on disk. Plus a mechanism candidate for BUG-1571
